title: Canonical prelude shape — markdown block, four fixed fields, capitalized labels
body:
The prelude is `## Target context
- Repo: <repo>
- Env: <env>
- Project: <project_or_none>
- Command: <count> (see structured target_context.commands_run)

` with a trailing blank line. Field order is fixed (Repo, Env, Project, Command). Labels are capitalized. All four lines are ALWAYS rendered — none are conditionally omitted. Special values: (a) when `target_context.project` is None / null / empty / the literal string 'none', the line renders as `- Project: (none)` for host-local plans (per F023 plan.md convention `target_project: none`); (b) `Command` (singular noun) shows the COUNT of `commands_run` plus a pointer to the structured field — no re-rendering of the command list. Why: (a) the structured target_context is the source of truth — re-rendering the full command list in prose would create two divergent surfaces; (b) capitalized labels match the user-facing convention from plan.md's `Target` section; (c) the explicit `(none)` for host-local plans distinguishes 'no project' from 'project missing' (the latter would fail validation per D004); (d) fixed four-field order makes the prelude byte-identical for byte-equal target_context inputs (required for F002 idempotence). How to apply: future fields added to target_context (e.g. credentials_scope) must explicitly opt-in to the prelude via a separate D-entry — the prelude shape does not auto-grow with the struct.

title: Repo precedence — struct first, cwd fallback, hard-fail on neither
body: Today's audit envelopes carry `target_context: {env, project, commands_run}` — `repo` is in F023's plan.md `Target` section convention but not always in every envelope's structured target_context. `render_prelude` resolves repo by precedence: (1) `target_context.repo` if present and non-empty; (2) basename of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from `os.getcwd()` at render time (read-only git call — no state mutation); (3) hard-fail with TargetContextError if neither yields a value. The fallback (2) is a transitional shim documented as such in the module: a future conventions-bump plan that adds `repo` as a required field in target_context will let the shim be removed. Why: (a) the user's prelude shape requires Repo always present; (b) hard-failing on missing repo today would break every existing envelope-construction call site (broader scope than this plan); (c) the cwd-derivation is deterministic + read-only + matches what the operator would manually fill in. How to apply: future schema-bump plan should remove the cwd shim and require `target_context.repo` upstream; until then, the shim is the platform's job, not the agent's.

title: Generation, not validation — supervisor injects the prelude rather than failing on missing prose
body: F002's audit_writer INJECTS the canonical prelude when struct is valid + prose is missing. The alternative considered — fail loudly on missing prose so the implementer regenerates with prelude — was rejected. Why: (a) failing on prose-missing trains agent attention onto a cosmetic format detail and burns a volley iteration on each occurrence; (b) the prelude is fully derivable from the structured field, so generation is the right primitive; (c) failing-on-prose is the failure mode this plan is fixing in the first place. How to apply: if a future need to validate prose content beyond the prelude appears (e.g. require a sign-off line), prefer generating it from structured input rather than asking agents to author it.

title: Hard-fail on invalid struct — no silent fallback
body: When `validate_target_context` raises (struct missing, env empty when commands ran, project empty when commands ran, commands without target metadata), F002's audit_writer raises `TargetContextError` and the envelope file does NOT land on disk. Alternative considered — write the envelope but tag it with a warning — rejected. Why: (a) a persisted envelope with invalid target_context is exactly the failure shape this plan exists to make impossible; (b) leaving the envelope on disk would let downstream stages (signoff, evidence packaging) consume it as if valid; (c) the hard fail surfaces the issue at the earliest possible moment, before audit_writer commits. How to apply: any future addition to target_context schema should also extend `validate_target_context` so the same hard-fail behavior covers the new fields.

title: Auditor severity is platform-enforced, not trust-based
body: F003's classifier downgrades EC5 severity at finding-aggregation time even if the auditor still files an i1. Alternative considered — trust the auditor's verdict and only update the prompt template — rejected. Why: (a) the auditor's prompt is best-effort context, not a contract; (b) prompt-only changes are slow to take effect and unreliable across agent vendors (Claude vs Codex vs future); (c) defensive classification at the platform layer means EC5 misfires can't slip through even on a vendor whose auditor is slow to internalize the rule. How to apply: any future severity rule that needs platform-enforcement should follow the same pattern (helper function called at finding-aggregation, before audit_writer persists).

title: No schema bump in this plan
body: The existing `audit.schema.json` (v1.0+) already carries the structured `target_context` field used by F023. This plan adds NO new schema fields. The canonical prelude is a constant in code + a render function; the classifier is a helper. If a future need surfaces (e.g. `summary_format_version` discriminator to track which envelopes have been platform-normalized vs legacy), that's a separate conventions-bump plan. Why: keep this plan small enough to land in 3 commits; schema bumps require agent-conventions repo bump + Pydantic model update + subtree pull (mirrors F023 EC1's three-step pattern). How to apply: when an EC5-class issue requires schema-level expressiveness, open a sibling conventions plan; do NOT retrofit this one.

title: Forward-only normalization — no historical envelope backfill
body: F002 does NOT migrate existing audit envelopes to inject preludes retroactively. Historical envelopes stay as-is. Alternative considered — write a one-shot script that walks docs/plans/*/audit/*.json and injects preludes — rejected. Why: (a) historical envelopes are evidence of what actually happened at audit time; rewriting them post-hoc would dilute audit-history integrity; (b) the platform's job is to make NEW envelopes correct, not to retcon old ones; (c) any analysis tool that needs canonical prelude on historical envelopes can apply `render_prelude(env.target_context)` at read time. How to apply: when F002 ships, the dashboard or any tool that reads historical envelopes for display should call render_prelude as a view-layer concern; do not rewrite stored data.

title: Severity downgrade preserves description text
body: F003's classifier mutates `severity` only, never `description`. When an auditor files an i1 EC5 finding with descriptive text and the classifier downgrades to i0, the description is preserved verbatim in the persisted envelope. Why: (a) the auditor's intent (what they thought was wrong) is recoverable for audit-history review even when the platform overrides their severity; (b) clobbering description would make it impossible to investigate auditor reasoning when severity rules later change; (c) preserving description maintains the adversarial-audit contract from D010 of the onboarding-ux plan — auditor claims are recorded even when the platform disagrees. How to apply: any future platform-enforced severity rule must follow the same convention — mutate severity, preserve description.

title: Plan does NOT bundle patch-completeness, delivery-profile, verifier-env, or role-volleys
body: Earlier scoping considered combining target-context fix with delivery-profile classifier (since both touch audit-envelope semantics). Rejected: (a) target-context fix is a bounded formatting/severity correction with clear acceptance; (b) delivery-profile is a much larger schema-and-supervisor change that would consume target-context semantics as one input among many; (c) bundling would create a 'too big to land' slice with mixed review needs. Why: each plan should justify its slicing in its own plan.md scope section. How to apply: future EC-class fixes (EC1-EC13 from F023) should follow the same independent-slice pattern — each one its own plan unless a tight semantic dependency exists.

title: F001 close-out — meta-recursive HIGH finding deferred to F002+F003 of this same plan
body: F001 ships passes:true with one residual HIGH finding from the dogfood volley: the implementer summary in claude-implementer-i1.json starts with `[F001] All three regressions resolved...` and lacks the canonical `Repo: Jarvis / Env: dev / Project: (none) / Command: <count>` prose prelude block. The structured `target_context` field is FULLY VALID (env='dev', project=None for host-local, commands_run populated with 7 entries) — only the prose rendering is missing. Per this plan's own D005 + F003 narrow downgrade rule, this is exactly the format-only case that should classify as i0 (struct valid + prose missing → format finding, not blocker). The auditor flagged it as HIGH because the platform fix is what THIS plan delivers: F002 ships audit_writer auto-injection of the canonical prelude from valid struct, F003 ships the auditor severity classifier that downgrades this case to i0 with description preservation. F001 only delivers helpers + fixtures (PRELUDE_TEMPLATE, render_prelude, validate_target_context, parse_prelude_block, TargetContextError) — the consuming surfaces are F002 + F003. Why defer rather than fix: editing the audit envelope post-hoc would fake the audit trail and destroy the evidence motivating F002+F003; F001 cannot contain its own consumers' fix without absorbing F002+F003's scope. Same shape as plan 2026-05-02-001-feat-resume-gate-discipline's D006 close-out (HIGH command-accountability deferred to this plan). How to apply: when F002's volley runs, the implementer summary will pass through F002's auto-injection on persist, removing this finding class entirely; F003's classifier provides the defensive downgrade for any remaining auditor false-positives. Evidence: 65/65 helper tests pass, 407/413 full suite (6 skipped pre-existing), ruff clean, sanitization clean (531 files). Audit trail: claude-implementer-i0/i1.json + codex-auditor-i0/i1.json preserved verbatim under audit/.

title: F002 close-out — Codex i1 remediation applied via manual cross-harness review
body: F002 volley terminated with i1 auditor findings (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, all test_coverage class). Operator ran a manual cross-harness review (paste F002 audit envelopes into Codex outside the volley harness) and Codex returned a remediation spec confirming all three are real locked-acceptance misses, not meta-platform classification issues. Each finding mapped to a specific test gap and was fixed verbatim against the auditor's exact text. (a) HIGH: case-c byte-equality must use the original F001 fixture (with documented sanitization transform), not a F002-owned writer-valid golden — Fix: `test_case_c_f001_fixture_byte_equality` in test_audit_writer_normalize.py asserts `_expected_serialized(loaded_fixture) == persisted_bytes` where `_load_fixture` applies the documented transform (drop `_fixture_notes`, substitute fixture-agent → claude, rebuild audit_id). The F002 golden file `evidence/f002/golden/case-c-writer-valid.json` was deleted to keep the F001 fixture as single source of truth. (b) MEDIUM: integration test must go through `cli.main(...)` and assert non-zero exit, not bare `supervisor.dispatch_volley` — Fix: `test_case_d_cli_main_returns_nonzero_on_invalid_target_context` invokes `cli.main([str(plan_dir), '--volley', '--feature', 'F001', '--max-iterations', '1'])`, captures the int return value, asserts != 0; TargetContextError is a ValueError subclass so cli.main's `except (FileNotFoundError, KeyError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc: return 1` path catches it cleanly. (c) LOW: forward-only proof was a 'non-persist supervisor cycle' that still called audit_writer.write on an unrelated envelope — Fix: strengthened to import-only, exercises render_prelude on a synthetic struct with NO call to audit_writer.write at all; snapshots historical envelope bytes AND mtime before/after to prove zero-touch (mtime changes even if a write-and-restore matches bytes, so this is the strict proof). Why manual cross-harness rather than the F002 auto-injection layer fixing itself: F002 cannot validate its own consumers' behavior — that's circular. The pattern matches D010 (F001 close-out) and 2026-05-02-001-feat-resume-gate-discipline D006 — when a plan fixes a gating signal, residual findings deferred to the consuming feature ship in the same plan. Test/lint state at remediation: 20/20 F002 targeted tests pass, 427 passed + 6 skipped full orchestrate suite, ruff clean, sanitization clean (538 files). Audit envelopes preserved verbatim under audit/ — implementer-i0/i1 + auditor-i0/i1 from the F002 volley reflect the platform's filename-collision finding (F002 envelopes overwrote committed F001 envelopes since filenames don't include feature_id). That filename-collision is its own platform finding, deferred to a follow-up plan; the audit trail history at HEAD `836c71d` preserves the F001 envelopes. How to apply: any future locked-acceptance miss surfaced by manual cross-harness review should follow this D-entry shape — list each finding's exact remediation, cite the test name + file, preserve audit envelopes verbatim (do NOT edit post-hoc), document any platform-level findings discovered along the way as separate deferred items.

title: F002 acceptance #3a clarification — case-c byte-equality is post-adaptation, not raw F001 fixture bytes
body: F002 confirmation volley auditor (codex-i1) repeatedly flagged HIGH test_coverage finding: `test_case_c_f001_fixture_byte_equality` does not compare against the F001 case-c fixture VERBATIM bytes — it sanitizes via `_load_fixture` (drops `_fixture_notes`, substitutes `agent: 'fixture-agent'` → `'claude'`, rebuilds `audit_id`) before computing expected bytes. Operator clarification (this D-entry): the literal-verbatim reading is structurally impossible against the current F001 fixture/model contract because (a) the Audit Pydantic model has `extra=forbid` so `_fixture_notes` cannot survive `Audit.model_validate`, and (b) the Agent enum does not include `'fixture-agent'` so the placeholder cannot survive validation either. Acceptance #3a's 'byte-equality vs source fixture' therefore means byte-equality AFTER the documented fixture-to-valid-envelope adaptation transform — exactly what `_load_fixture` + `_expected_serialized` implement. Why we don't fix it 'the auditor's way': rewriting the F001 fixture (case-c) to be writer-valid (no `_fixture_notes`, real Agent enum) would mutate already-signed-off F001 evidence to satisfy F002's auditor — the wrong direction. F001 fixtures are intentionally annotated with `_fixture_notes` (acceptance #9 of F001) to document each case's expected outcomes for both F002 and F003; stripping them would destroy that annotation. The auditor's reading is internally consistent but conflicts with F001's explicit acceptance. How to apply: any future test that asserts byte-equality against an F001-style fixture must apply the same documented sanitization transform; the contract is 'byte-equality after the documented adaptation,' not 'byte-equality of raw fixture file bytes.' Companion remediations on the same volley round: MEDIUM (correctness — `_normalize_summary` used header-only `lstrip().startswith()` check, allowing malformed-block to false-positive as no-op) was a real defect and was fixed by switching to `parse_prelude_block`-based detection (returns dict for full canonical block including case-g value-mismatch; returns None for no-prelude → inject; raises for malformed-prelude → no-partial-artifact raise). LOW (forward-only proof) was a regression I introduced when removing the unrelated-envelope `audit_writer.write` call; restored it while keeping the historical bytes+mtime stability assertions and the supervisor read-only cycle (`circuit_breakers.check_diminishing_returns` / `check_convergence_collapse`) the confirmation-volley implementer added.

title: Deferred follow-up — audit envelope filename collision across features within a plan
body: Discovered during F002 confirmation volley: audit envelope filenames are `{agent}-{role}-i{n}.json` per F005a-1, with no feature_id. When a single plan ships multiple features (this plan: F001, F002, F003) and each feature's volley persists envelopes under the same `audit/` directory, the LATER volley overwrites the EARLIER volley's envelopes. Concretely on this plan: F002's volley overwrote F001's i0+i1 envelopes in working tree (F001 versions preserved in git history at commit 836c71d / `Add target context prelude helpers`). Mitigated for this plan by copying the F002 originals to `evidence/f002/audit-original-volley/` before running the F002 confirmation volley. The clean platform fix is: include feature_id in the audit filename, e.g. `{agent}-{role}-{feature_id}-i{n}.json`. This is a small platform plan (probably 1 feature, ≤ 3 files: audit_writer.py filename pattern + supervisor.dispatch_volley wiring + a regression test). Slotted AFTER plan 005 F003 close-out per operator queue order (F003 may touch audit/finding semantics and can inform filename shape). NOT slotted before F003. Why defer rather than fix now: (a) F002 close-out is the active commit boundary; broadening to filename refactor would expand scope; (b) F003 will exercise audit_writer/finding paths and may surface adjacent shape needs; (c) the workaround (manual copy to evidence/) is acceptable for a single dogfood instance. How to apply: when drafting the follow-up plan, treat as a tier=trivial infra plan; reference D013 in the new plan's motivation; ensure the change is forward-only (existing envelope filenames stay valid; new envelopes use the new pattern); update the F005a-1 D-entry once landed.

title: F003 close-out — direct path (no volley) for the EC5 severity classifier
body: F003 shipped via TDD red→green direct path — no volley dispatched. Operator-approved on 2026-05-02 after F002 close-out. Rationale: F003's deliverable is a small, well-bounded platform patch (~140 lines pure helper + 5-line wiring + 1 prompt paragraph) with acceptance heavily clarified across D005/D008/D010/D011/D012 over the prior 12 hours. F002's two volleys already produced the relevant adversarial cases on the EC5 surface (header-only false-positive no-op → drove F002's parse_prelude_block fix; verbatim case-c byte-eq → D012 structural-impossibility clarification; forward-only proof regression → D012 LOW restoration). Per the volley failure-taxonomy memory captured during F002 close-out, additional volleys on a saturated, well-bounded surface are more likely to produce interpretive_disagreement-class findings than feature_defect-class — testing review-loop instability rather than implementation. Direct path delivered: ec5_classifier.py (pure helpers — classify_ec5_severity, is_ec5_finding, apply_ec5_classifier_to_findings); audit_writer.build_audit calls aggregator after finding extraction and before _derive_status; EC5_AUDITOR_RULE paragraph embedded in auditor_prompt with explicit value-mismatch carve-out. Schema unchanged per D006 — abstract 'i0' verdict maps to existing 'advisory' severity at the aggregation boundary. Description preservation per D008 — only severity mutates, all other finding fields survive verbatim. Backwards-compat per acceptance #10 — legacy findings without explicit code field detected via regex anchored on 'target<sep>context...prelude' bigram. Test/lint state at close-out: 19/19 F003 targeted tests pass, 447 passed + 6 skipped full orchestrate suite (was 428 → +19 F003 tests), ruff clean, sanitization clean (544 files). No agent retraining — prompt-as-context change only; supervisor classifier defensively re-applies the rule at aggregation so vendors slow to internalize still produce correct severity (D005). How to apply: future small, well-bounded platform patches with heavily-clarified acceptance and prior adversarial saturation should follow this direct-path pattern; the volley failure-taxonomy memory documents the trigger conditions. Plan 005 fully closed after this commit (F001+F002+F003 all passes:true). Queued follow-ups (operator order): audit-filename collision plan (D013) → nested-orchestration plan.

title: Schema-conformance repair — features[1].evidence_refs[4].type 'dir' → 'audit_json' (validator preflight at status-flip close-out)
body:
Validator preflight during the status-flip close-out (2026-05-07) surfaced one schema violation in features.json: features[1] (F002) evidence_refs[4] had `type='dir'`, which is not in the v1.0 schema enum (`screenshot | log | test_output | diff | audit_json | commit | url | file`). The URI points to `evidence/f002/audit-original-volley/`, a directory containing 4 preserved audit envelope JSONs from the original F002 volley (per D011/D013 — preserved verbatim before F002 confirmation-volley overwrote them due to filename collision).

Operator-approved repair (Path A — validator-conformance, not historical reinterpretation): change ONLY `features[1].evidence_refs[4].type` from `'dir'` to `'audit_json'` (the closest valid enum value matching the artifact contents — directory of audit envelope JSONs). `uri`, `captured_by`, and `note` preserved verbatim.

Why this repair is appropriate at close-out rather than retro-update-history-as-drift:
1. The field was schema-invalid under v1.0 from ship-time — validator would have rejected it whenever first run against this dir. This is not 'AC was true at ship time, became drift' (the brand-rename pattern); this is 'AC was never schema-conformant.' Schema-history check via git was blocked by the partial-clone `1db24649` corruption, but the current schema enum is consistent with what v1.0 has shipped — `'dir'` was never valid under any known v1.0 revision.
2. The URI points to preserved audit envelope JSONs (`evidence/f002/audit-original-volley/{claude-implementer-i0,claude-implementer-i1,codex-auditor-i0,codex-auditor-i1}.json`) — `audit_json` matches both the filename pattern and the on-disk content exactly. No semantic invention: the type label is now consistent with what the URI points to.
3. No acceptance claim, status, or evidence content changed. The file still references the same directory; the same artifacts are still preserved; the same note explains why; the same captured_by attributes the capture. Only the schema-enum label was corrected.
4. Operator-approved at close-out turn under explicit Path A directive: 'This is validation-conformance repair, not historical reinterpretation. The historical claim is not being changed; the evidence ref is being made schema-valid so the already-stated evidence can be represented correctly.'

Repair mechanics: byte-stable surgical edit via single literal-string replacement (`'"type": "dir"'` → `'"type": "audit_json"'`). Diff size: exactly 1 insertion + 1 deletion at line 175. Byte size delta: +7 (matches len(replacement) - len(needle) exactly). Unicode-escape encoding (e.g. `\u2014` for em-dashes) preserved throughout the rest of the file. Validator now passes.

Scope discipline (operator-explicit at the repair turn): 'Do not broaden this into an all-plans schema-debt sweep inside this close-out. Plan 2026-05-04-002 or any broader legacy evidence-ref repair should stay separate.' This entry is therefore narrowly scoped to Plan 005's single-field violation. If similar `type='dir'` (or other schema-invalid evidence_refs) exist in other active plans, they remain separate close-outs to address.

How to apply: future close-out preflight (Step 1c content-size verification + Step 2 validate) catches this class of violation. When found, apply the same Path A discipline: surface to operator, propose narrow repair, apply only with operator approval, document in a D-entry, do NOT broaden to other plans within the same commit. The D-entry preserves the audit trail of WHAT was repaired, WHY it was repair-not-rewrite, and WHO approved it — same shape as any other historical-record update.
